stem:
Yash says a whole number is divisible by 10 exactly when its units digit is 0.

Why does this last-digit shortcut work?

options.text: Units digit is the name of the rule, so that label is the reason.
The units digit produces place value, so place value comes from the units digit alone.
Every higher place value in a whole number is a multiple of 10, so only the units digit can affect divisibility by 10.
The answer is place value because those words are the most obvious label in the idea.

teacher.key_rationale: Expanding by place value, tens and above are multiples of 10, so divisibility by 10 depends only on the units digit. Naming units digit is not a reason. Place value is not produced by the units digit. Grabbing the words place value skips the expansion argument.
